design_assumptions: Grid-fin stowed frontal blockage: stowed fin treated as a flat fairing of frontal area planform * (t/c), t/c = 0.12 (lattice truss depth over chord) -- DESIGN ASSUMPTION from E11-01 photos, +/-50 % on t/c, which propagates linearly into the stowed increment.
Protuberance interference factor K = 1.9 (Hoerner fairing-body interference) -- DESIGN ASSUMPTION, range 1.5..2.3.
Engines-first aft face effective area fraction 0.85 of the body cross-section (engine gimbal ring + landing-leg recesses cover the rest) -- DESIGN ASSUMPTION, +/-10 %.

Subsonic/low-supersonic forward base treated as a flat carry-deck base (DESIGN ASSUMPTION: (full suction, Missile DATCOM base term) -- the real forward end is a shallow cavity, so the true base drag is smaller; the table errs high in subsonic Cd by up to ~0.05.

sources.detail: orbitopt.flightlab.nose_aero: Taylor-Maccoll cone/ogive wave drag, Rayleigh pitot Cp, Prandtl-Glauert corrected turbulent Cf, DATCOM power-off base term -- the repo's own semi-empirical aero generator.
vehicle grid_fins block (cd_add_mach / cn_alpha_mach), provenance public_estimate, derivation in docs/benchmarks/e11_01_grid_fin_authority.md.

tests/data/mission/reference/e5-08-new-vehicle-starbase/.../stage1_debris.csv and the DC7 twin: an in-flight power-off Cd inversion is public data in the strongest sense the repo holds -- a measured trajectory of the actual model.
f9_class_public_estimate.yaml declares ballistic_coefficient_kg_m2 for the booster stage; m/(Cd*S) at the declared masses bounds the power-off Cd from published empty-mass and diameter figures.

part_b_recorded_inversion.method: central difference of recorded ECEF velocity, gravity (J2) + Coriolis + centrifugal removed with the twin's own force package, projected on -v_rel; Cd = m a / (q S) with the recorded q; rows with q > 50 kPa

part_d_fin_state.note: deployed at zero incidence = profile + blockage; at flying alpha the E11-01 envelope adds the normal-force and induced terms on top (docs/benchmarks/e11_01_grid_fin_authority.md)

verdict.conclusion: the qualified power-off model leaves the Starbase debris check outside the unchanged 12 % band (replay +12.70 %), so the discrepancy stays recorded as a genuine aero-model difference; the new evidence narrows WHERE it lives: the recorded flights invert to a power-off Cd BELOW the declared polar (Starbase 0.960, DC7 0.934), so no physically supported power-off correction (protuberances +, deployed fins +) closes it -- every build-up term moves the replay FURTHER out; the remaining gap is the aero/atmosphere line between OT and the twin in dense high-q air, not a booster Cd error
